five_small_module_review: Generic GBA Flash-chip hardware operations: unlock/read-ID, bank switching, copied Thumb routines for volatile reads/verification, timer interrupts, sector program/verify retries and wait-state changes. Browser saves use localStorage, with no mapped flash bus/registers; this module has no direct game rules. Excludes physical flash behavior only; browser save reliability and corruption handling require separate parity review.

This module identifies the physical 1 Mbit GBA flash chip, switches register timing, assigns chip-specific flash driver callbacks, and polls hardware writes. The browser persists saves through localStorage and has no flash chip or memory-mapped register equivalent. Classification excludes only this physical-device driver, not save-flow or save-format parity.

This file only configures the LE26FV10N1TS GBA flash chip timings, sector geometry and hardware IDs. The browser save adapter uses localStorage, so this device-specific driver has no web runtime analogue. This classification does not assert byte-for-byte SaveBlock or save-UI parity.

Contains MX29L010/DefaultFlash chip geometry and the physical GBA flash command sequences for chip/sector erase, byte/sector program, wait-state switching, bank switching and timer-polled writes. Web saves use localStorage; this device driver has no web runtime analogue. Excludes only physical Flash operations, not save semantics.

ReloadSave is only called by link.c/RFU link recovery paths. Its EWRAM/register reset and SaveBlock reload are hardware/link recovery, not part of single-player progression; the browser save/continue path is implemented separately. This does not claim byte-level SaveBlock parity.

roamer.ts now distinguishes warp/continue movement (new location set) from camera-transition RoamerMove (1/16 set change), updates history in both paths, and mirrors source post-battle outcomes exactly: WON/CAUGHT/DREW deactivate; TELEPORTED does not. Calls are wired from Game.continueGame and the two overworld map-load paths. npm run check:port passed. No browser/encounter simulation in this source-review pass.

Defines a static Game Freak metadata/offset table with SaveBlock offsets and pointers to C data for external ROM consumers. Repository search finds no FireRed runtime caller; it is an integration header for external tools/services, not single-player game behavior. Classification applies only to this metadata export.

Reviewed all eight public APIs across TS modules: flag get/set/reset, enter/exit with 30 balls/600 steps/stat, step timeout script, retire prompt, and post-battle outcomes/warp paths. Function names are split across specials, Game, FieldEffects and battleSetup. Source-review parity; no Safari Zone browser playthrough was run.

Implements recovery UI and retry logic for physically damaged GBA Flash sectors using ReadFlash, ProgramFlashByte, sector erase/rewrite and save callbacks. Browser saves use localStorage and have no sectors or flash chip to repair. Excludes this hardware recovery screen only; corrupted, unavailable or incompatible browser save handling is not thereby proven equivalent.

Reviewed against save_location.c and load_save.c: browser stores the current warp directly and continues from it; missing specialSaveWarpFlags cover Pokémon Center/lobby reset warps, GameCube link unlocks, and Champion/postgame behavior. No normal main-story single-player blocker found; defer until reset/link/postgame parity.

Game.startMenuSave now renders source-derived location, player, badges, Pokédex and time values in a stats panel before confirmation. Simplified Canvas window/color handling; exact palette/text control parity still unverified.

TS hw/scanline.ts implements the 16/32-bit HBlank DMA register path, double buffers, stop/clear/params, first-line+per-scanline PPU writes, wave task, sine generation and optional battle BG offsets. Call path is wired into the PPU scanline renderer. Source-to-TS review only; no frame-by-frame visual comparison in this pass.

Bytecode/native context, call stack, immediate/global execution and map-script table runners are represented in script/context.ts and overworld.ts; command handlers are separate in commands.ts. C RAM-script magic/checksum/save-persistence, saved wonder-card script validation, signpost/cancel flags, and Quest Log input recorder helpers lack complete equivalents. Marked partial; 213 handler registration is not proof of behavior.

StartObjectMovementScript resolves the requested map object and returns C's failure/pending state; repeated starts, script-slot capacity/reuse, per-frame held-movement waits, pointer advancement, STEP_END freeze, is-finished checks and unfreeze/stop are represented by script/movement.ts using object references instead of C task.data packed IDs. Source-reviewed only; timing and task-table interactions were not run.

HealPlayerParty and DoesPartyHaveEnigmaBerry have TS special handlers; HasEnoughMonsForDoubleBattle previously collapsed the C three-state result and now returns PLAYER_HAS_ONE_MON for a one-slot party, otherwise TWO_USABLE or ONE_USABLE based on living non-eggs. ScriptGiveMon, ScriptGiveEgg, ScriptSetMonMoveSlot, CreateScriptedWildMon have no same-name TS functions; party menu selection hooks remain no-ops in specials.ts. Source review only; compile check pending.

Ferry setup state machine, route bitmap/table, direction/number, water scroll, ferry/wake animation, palette fade, destination menu selection and final warp are ported in seagallop.ts with exported source assets. Adapted to Canvas/WebAudio; no frame-by-frame visual comparison was run.

Revision-10 Sloop emulator SWI bridge for RFU/link state, emulator save sectors/finish-save, parental communication controls, bad-word service, starter/activity telemetry and link-error counters. These syscalls are supplied by the emulator rather than the FireRed gameplay runtime; the web port uses browser storage and has no RFU/Sloop services. No single-player rule implementation is in this module.

Map music state, fades/fanfares, SEs, cry modes, pitch/pan/ducking and wait/playing state have browser counterparts in audio/sound.ts and m4a.ts, but output uses a WebAudio sequencer rather than the GBA M4A engine; source music/effect fidelity remains incomplete. Marked partial for behavior/render fidelity; no audio comparison.

StartEscalator/StopEscalator/IsEscalatorMoving animate 3x3 escalator metatiles over three transition stages via field tasks; no equivalent task/visual choreography found in TS, though escalator warp routing exists. AnimateTeleporterHousing and AnimateTeleporterCable are explicit no-op specials in specials.ts; source changes specific Sea Cottage metatiles over 13x16-frame and 4x4-frame sequences. Source-backed gameplay/visual gaps; not ported.

The 50-frame horn delay, loaded wake/smoke frame data, 70-frame smoke interval, boat x2 drift at floor(frame/5), offscreen threshold, second horn, 40-frame finish delay and script resume are mapped in specialsExtra.ts. Sprite sizes, animation frame durations and callbacks match C using Canvas field sprites. Source-reviewed; no visual timing comparison.

Core GBA byte-string operations are spread across gba/charmap.ts, textPrinter.ts and battle/message.ts: copy/concat/length, decimal formatting, control-code length, general and battle placeholder expansion. No source-equivalent Braille-string formatter found (Braille has its own partial adapter); Japanese/international conversion and all multibyte/control-code comparison helpers are not exhaustively represented. Partial source/API audit; no parity vectors run.

Reworked gba/tasks.ts to match C's linked priority order and stable insertion order (including reused slot IDs), traversal during callbacks and destroy, reset data/state, 16-slot exhaustion behavior, task queries/count and 32-bit word args. Followup callbacks are stored as JS function references rather than split pointer halfwords in data[14:16], preserving behavior in web. npm run check:port passes; no frame-order comparison was run.
The six program labels and narration flow are adapted in menus/keyItemScreens.ts. GBA graphics, menu behavior and the Pokédude battle controller remain unported.

Printer state machine/control codes/colors/delays/scroll/prompt are implemented across gba/textPrinter.ts and hw/text.ts. Source ClearTextSpan is an empty stub; changed TS clearSpan to no-op to match it. Glyph rasterization uses exported web font data rather than GBA tile lookup/half-row VRAM copying; Braille custom glyph path remains missing (tracked under braille_text.c). npm run check:port passed; no pixel/frame comparison.

Standard/user/menu frame graphics and palettes, GetTextWindowPalette, dialogue frames, and outer text borders are represented in hw/menu.ts and menuHelpers.ts using exported C frame data. No TS equivalents for LoadSignpostWindowGfx, LoadQuestLogWindowTiles, DrawTextBorderInner, or rbox_fill_rectangle; field signpost/window rendering also uses Canvas2D adaptation.

All cdata/incbin definitions are exported. GetUserWindowGraphics is implemented in hw/menu.ts with the C out-of-range fallback to frame 0; user-frame loaders and standard text-window tiles/palettes consume the exported symbols. No separate pixel parity comparison of every frame was run.

Implements rectangle/position copying for the PKMN Data, party-menu and close-box tilemaps in pokemon_storage_system_tasks.c, including the sliding party menu and alternating close-box states. The web storage UI is still a menu adapter and does not render these source tilemaps or call TilemapUtil. Optional PC box presentation only; no effect on party/battle progression. Source review only.

TilesetAnimator in field/tileRenderer.ts covers all six C callbacks, frame arrays/order, destinations/counts, modulo periods and frame counters. Canvas writes tiles immediately instead of queued DMA3; prime() draws initial frames on load. Source/timing review only; no browser or pixel comparison.

This compilation unit contains no functions; it includes the authoritative graphics, metatile and tileset-header tables. tools/decomp/step_tilesets.py exports those C declarations/assets into public/fr/tilesets, and rom.loadTileset consumes the generated map tilesets. Reviewed as data-path parity for this file; tileset callbacks and visual/runtime parity have separate coverage.

Postgame fan bits/timer, initial three fans and Saffron NPC visibility, periodic gain/loss, count/member checks and NPC name buffering are implemented in specialsExtra.ts. ResetTrainerFanClub and link-battle-only paths (fan gain/loss and link record names) are absent; no local link battles. Source logic reviewed; no play-time/event integration verification.

Picture-table decompression/palette primitives are implemented in pokemon/pics.ts and trainer/battler rendering uses cdata elsewhere; trainer card draws the player image from exported C sheets. The full eight-slot CreatePicSprite ownership/lifecycle API is absent, and battle DexScreen CreateMonPicSprite_HandleDeoxys remains a 0xffff stub while the Pokedex UI is an adapter. Source review only; these presentation paths are not full C-equivalent.

Both source sine tables are exported and loaded by hw/trig.ts; Sin/Cos Q8.8 multiplication, Sin2/Cos2 degree reflection and signed behavior are represented. ArcTan2 helpers add BIOS-compatible functions outside this C file. Reviewed source mapping; no exhaustive numeric diff generated this pass.

Several primitives are mapped elsewhere: BlendPalette in hw/palette.ts, DoBgAffineSet core math in hw/bg.ts, CountTrailingZeroBits inline in battle/util.ts, and paired task data adapted to TS references. CopySpriteTiles and CRC16/table/byte sum APIs are absent; CRC/sum callers are RAM-script/Mystery Event/trainer-tower transfer validation, outside the normal single-player path. No same-stem TS module; review split by call path, no runtime checks.

Added getSpeciesPokedexAreaMarkers logic in src/fr/pokedexArea.ts using exported wild encounter and MAPSEC/DEX_AREA cdata; covers roamer starter/location, unlock flags and selected Altering Cave table. Shared with marker descriptor helper; runtime check and UI wiring remain.

Window allocation, tilemaps, bitmap drawing, fills, scrolling, attributes and copy-to-VRAM paths are split across gba/window.ts and hw/window.ts; screen consumers use both layers. Several source entry points/8-bit APIs lack direct equivalents, and memory allocation is JS-managed. Marked partial; no full API parity or pixel comparison.

No TS 8bpp window lifecycle APIs yet: AddWindow8Bit, FillWindowPixelBuffer8Bit, FillWindowPixelRect8Bit, BlitBitmapRectToWindow4BitTo8Bit wrapper, and CopyWindowToVram8Bit. Source review only.

Counts RFU wireless trade, battle, union-room and wireless minigame activity, displays connected peers and cycles status palettes. No single-player caller; RFU/link hardware absent. Out of scope for single-player mode.

Manages reward berries and step-gated reward limits for Wonder News sent to/received from link partners; it requires saved Mystery Gift Wonder News and link/distribution data. The web single-player route has no Wonder News transfer or acquisition path; its existing handler returns no reward. Excludes this link-distribution reward subsystem only.
